messages.author: Merc Fredis
messages.content:
heh, i asked AI about the VOIP problem and ran GZW a few times with a bunch of WINEDEBUG variables set, it came up with:


In plain language: the voice networking code creates an IPv4 socket, asks it about an IPv6-specific property, receives “operation not supported,” and abandons the socket. IPV6_V6ONLY describes whether an IPv6 socket also accepts IPv4 traffic.

GZW 0.5 VOIP under GE-Proton11-11 fails during ODIN socket initialization. An AF_INET/SOCK_DGRAM socket is successfully created and bound, then queried with getsockopt(IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_V6ONLY). Wine returns STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED, mapped to WSAEOPNOTSUPP/10045. The socket is immediately closed, and ODIN reports room connection closed 10 ms later. GZW 0.4 VOIP worked on Linux.

Seems the issue is related to IPv6.   Don't kill me Blu.    hear me out. 

I enabled logging for odin in engine.ini and start sniffing around to what was going on.

in windows, when there was no ip6, it reports that it's not there.(response V6ONLY=0)
in linux.. it's reporting not supported ( STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED  |  error 10045).. so odin is dropping the connection.  It wasn't returning the error level it expected. 

I patched the wine ws2_32.dll to change the error message to mimic windows and I am able to join the odin rooms, and communicate with folks in game now. (edited)

messages.content:
The short of it.   If you see the mic icon, then you're connected to the odin lobby, and it is working for you.     The problem was the wine layer giving an 'invalid' response to odin (in regards to whether or not ip6 was a valid route) when handshaking.   When it didn't give you a valid response, it didn't let you into the chat. 

So,  if you see the icon now, you're in the chat.. and you're good to go.  If you still have issues after that, that's going to be a configuration issue with your microphone/machine/pulse/pipewire/etc.

messages.author: k3LLerInstInkt
messages.content:
In my case on CachyOS, I copied the system Proton install to a user-writable location instead of patching it in place (the system copy is root-owned, read-only, and managed by pacman, so an update would overwrite the patch):


cp -a /usr/share/steam/compatibilitytools.d/proton-cachyos-slr ~/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d/proton-cachyos-slr-gzw


Then edit ~/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d/proton-cachyos-slr-gzw/compatibilitytool.vdf and change both the internal tool name and the display name, so the copy doesn't clash with the system install:


"proton-cachyos-slr"  ->  "proton-cachyos-slr-gzw"

"display_name" "proton-cachyos-11.0-20261015 (steam linux runtime)"
->
"display_name" "proton-cachyos-slr-gzw (GZW VOIP-Patch)"


Check, patch, check again:


python gzw_voip_fix-autodetect.py --dll ~/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d/proton-cachyos-slr-gzw/files/lib/wine/x86_64-windows/ws2_32.dll --check
python gzw_voip_fix-autodetect.py --dll ~/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d/proton-cachyos-slr-gzw/files/lib/wine/x86_64-windows/ws2_32.dll
python gzw_voip_fix-autodetect.py --dll ~/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d/proton-cachyos-slr-gzw/files/lib/wine/x86_64-windows/ws2_32.dll --check


The first check should report CLEAN, the last one PATCHED.

Restart Steam, then select the new tool under the game's Properties → Compatibility.
